plates.caption: Steel engraving by J. L. Raab (1869) after Wilhelm von Kaulbach's Hunnenschlacht: the dead of a battle against Attila fight on in the air, after a story told by the philosopher Damascius. Kaulbach's picture (1834–37) and Liszt's symphonic poem made the battle a scene of nineteenth-century art.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:Die Hunnenschlacht Raab nach Wilhelm von Kaulbach.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Die_Hunnenschlacht_Raab_nach_Wilhelm_von_Kaulbach.jpg)

plates.titel: The Roman and Hunnic empires about 450
plates.caption: William R. Shepherd, Historical Atlas (1911). A modern map of the empires on the eve of Attila's march into Gaul.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:C. 450 Roman and Hun Empires.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:C._450_Roman_and_Hun_Empires.jpg)

plates.caption: William R. Shepherd, Historical Atlas (1911): the Germanic kingdoms in Gaul, among them the Visigoths of Toulouse and the Burgundians, whose warriors fought in 451.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:C. 450 Germanic invasions of Gaul.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:C._450_Germanic_invasions_of_Gaul.jpg)

plates.titel: King Attila's battle on the Catalaunian plain
plates.caption: Woodcut from the Chronicle of János Thuróczy (Augsburg 1488), where Attila is the first king of the Hungarians: the battle as Hungarian history told it.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:Thuróczy krónika - Attila király csatája a catalaunumi síkon.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Thur%C3%B3czy_kr%C3%B3nika_-_Attila_kir%C3%A1ly_csat%C3%A1ja_a_catalaunumi_s%C3%ADkon.jpg)

plates.caption: Mór Than, Attila lakomája (1870), Hungarian National Gallery: the banquet Priscus describes, painted for a Hungarian public for whom Attila was an ancestral king. Attila sits with his wooden cup among guests served from silver.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:Than Mór - Attila lakomája (1870).jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Than_M%C3%B3r_-_Attila_lakom%C3%A1ja_(1870).jpg)

plates.caption: Engraving after Giovanni Strozza (18th century). No likeness of Aetius survives that can be shown here: this portrait is an invention of the early modern print trade, as are most images of him.

Raphael, fresco in the Stanza di Eliodoro, Vatican (1514). Pope Leo meets Attila on the Mincio in 452; Peter and Paul appear in the sky with swords. The meeting is in Prosper's chronicle; the apostles are Raphael's.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:Raphael - The Meeting of Leo the Great and Attila.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Raphael_-_The_Meeting_of_Leo_the_Great_and_Attila.jpg)

plates.titel: Saint Lupus stops Attila before Troyes
plates.caption: Colour lithograph by E. Crété after H. Grobet (1902). The Life of Lupus, which the editor Bruno Krusch judged a late invention, made the bishop of Troyes the man who faced Attila.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:H. Grobet - Saint Loup arrête Attila devant Troyes (451).jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:H._Grobet_-_Saint_Loup_arr%C3%AAte_Attila_devant_Troyes_(451).jpg)

plates.caption: Pierre Puvis de Chavannes, Sainte Geneviève veillant sur Paris, a version of his last panel for the Panthéon (1898), Musée du Grand Siècle. The old Genovefa watches over the sleeping city by night; the Life of Genovefa itself has her keep the Parisians from fleeing in 451.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:Puvis de Chavannes - Sainte Geneviève veillant sur Paris.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Puvis_de_Chavannes_-_Sainte_Genevi%C3%A8ve_veillant_sur_Paris.jpg)

plates.caption: Stained glass, cathedral of Meaux (1869): Genovefa kneels before a crowned Attila on horseback. The meeting is the window's: in the Life of Genovefa she never sees him, and her quarrel is with the citizens of Paris.
plates.source: Wikimedia Commons, File:Meaux Vitrail 1869 4 Ste Geneviève et Attila.jpg (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Meaux_Vitrail_1869_4_Ste_Genevi%C3%A8ve_et_Attila.jpg)
